sanskrit: tad icchāmi parāṃ buddhiṃ śrotuṃ bharatasattama yathā rājan na muhyeta śatrubhiḥ parivāritaḥ
english: This I wish to hear, O best of the Bhāratas: that supreme wisdom by which a king, though surrounded by enemies, would not lose his way.

sanskrit: dharmārthakuśala prājña sarvaśāstraviśārada pṛcchāmi tvā kuruśreṣṭha tan me vyākhyātum arhasi
english: O you who are skilled in dharma and statecraft, wise one, master of all the śāstras, I ask you, best of the Kurus; you ought to expound this to me.

sanskrit: śatrubhir bahubhir grasto yathā varteta pārthivaḥ etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ sarvam eva yathāvidhi
english: How a king beset by many foes should conduct himself—this I wish to hear, all of it, in proper order.

sanskrit: viṣamasthaṃ hi rājānaṃ śatravaḥ paripanthinaḥ bahavo 'py ekam uddhartuṃ yatante pūrvatāpitāḥ
english: For when a king stands in difficult straits, his hostile enemies—many against one—strive to root him out, inflamed by earlier injuries.

sanskrit: sarvataḥ prārthyamānena durbalena mahābalaiḥ ekenaivāsahāyena śakyaṃ sthātuṃ kathaṃ bhavet
english: Pressed on every side, weak against the mighty, alone and without help—how could such a one possibly hold his ground?

sanskrit: kathaṃ mitram ariṃ caiva vindeta bharatarṣabha ceṣṭitavyaṃ kathaṃ cātra śatror mitrasya cāntare
english: How, O bull of the Bhāratas, should he tell friend from foe, and how should he act in the space between an enemy and a friend?

sanskrit: prajñātalakṣaṇe rājann amitre mitratāṃ gate kathaṃ nu puruṣaḥ kuryāt kiṃ vā kṛtvā sukhī bhavet
english: When, O king, an enemy of well-known character turns to friendship, what should a man do, and by doing what would he be at ease?

sanskrit: vigrahaṃ kena vā kuryāt saṃdhiṃ vā kena yojayet kathaṃ vā śatrumadhyastho vartetābalavān iti
english: With whom should he make war, and with whom should he forge a treaty, and how should one without strength conduct himself when set in the midst of enemies?

sanskrit: etad vai sarvakṛtyānāṃ paraṃ kṛtyaṃ paraṃtapa naitasya kaś cid vaktāsti śrotā cāpi sudurlabhaḥ
english: This, O scorcher of foes, is the highest of all matters of action; yet there is none who can speak of it, and one who can grasp it is hard indeed to find.

sanskrit: ṛte śāṃtanavād bhīṣmāt satyasaṃdhāj jitendriyāt tad anviṣya mahābāho sarvam etad vadasva me
english: None save Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, true to his word and master of his senses—so search it out, O mighty-armed one, and tell me all of this.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tvadyukto 'yam anupraśno yudhiṣṭhira guṇodayaḥ śṛṇu me putra kārtsnyena guhyam āpatsu bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: This follow-up question befits you, Yudhiṣṭhira, and is rich in merit. Hear from me in full, my son, the secret to be observed in times of distress, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: amitro mitratāṃ yāti mitraṃ cāpi praduṣyati sāmarthyayogāt kāryāṇāṃ tadgatyā hi sadā gatiḥ
english: An enemy turns into a friend, and a friend too turns hostile, according as interests align; for the course of things forever follows that course.

sanskrit: tasmād viśvasitavyaṃ ca vigrahaṃ ca samācaret deśaṃ kālaṃ ca vijñāya kāryākāryaviniścaye
english: Therefore one should both place trust and wage war, having weighed place and time in deciding what is to be done and what is not.

sanskrit: saṃdhātavyaṃ budhair nityaṃ vyavasyaṃ ca hitārthibhiḥ amitrair api saṃdheyaṃ prāṇā rakṣyāś ca bhārata
english: The wise who seek their own good should always be ready both to make peace and to take resolute action; even with enemies one may make a treaty, and one's life must be guarded, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: yo hy amitrair naro nityaṃ na saṃdadhyād apaṇḍitaḥ na so 'rtham āpnuyāt kiṃ cit phalāny api ca bhārata
english: For the foolish man who would never make terms with his enemies gains no advantage whatsoever, nor any fruit, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: yas tv amitreṇa saṃdhatte mitreṇa ca virudhyate arthayuktiṃ samālokya sumahad vindate phalam
english: But he who makes a pact with an enemy and breaks with a friend, looking to where his interest lies, wins a very great reward.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam mārjārasya ca saṃvādaṃ nyagrodhe mūṣakasya ca
english: On this they relate an ancient tale, the dialogue of a cat and a mouse upon a banyan tree.

sanskrit: vane mahati kasmiṃś cin nyagrodhaḥ sumahān abhūt latājālaparicchanno nānādvijagaṇāyutaḥ
english: In a certain great forest there stood a mighty banyan, screened by a network of creepers and thronged with flocks of many kinds of birds.

sanskrit: skandhavān meghasaṃkāśaḥ śītacchāyo manoramaḥ vairantyam abhito jātas tarur vyālamṛgākulaḥ
english: Broad of trunk, like a cloud in mass, cool of shade and lovely, the tree had grown up near a wilderness and was haunted by beasts of prey.

sanskrit: tasya mūlaṃ samāśritya kṛtvā śatamukhaṃ bilam vasati sma mahāprājñaḥ palito nāma mūṣakaḥ
english: Sheltering at its root, having made himself a burrow with a hundred mouths, there dwelt a very wise mouse named Palita.

sanskrit: śākhāś ca tasya saṃśritya vasati sma sukhaṃ puraḥ lomaśo nāma mārjāraḥ pakṣisattvāvasādakaḥ
english: And taking to its branches there dwelt at ease above a cat named Lomaśa, a destroyer of birds and other creatures.

sanskrit: tatra cāgatya caṇḍālo vairantyakṛtaketanaḥ ayojayat tam unmāthaṃ nityam astaṃ gate ravau
english: Now there came a hunter who had made his dwelling in that wilderness, and every day, when the sun had set, he would set his snare.

sanskrit: tatra snāyumayān pāśān yathāvat saṃnidhāya saḥ gṛhaṃ gatvā sukhaṃ śete prabhātām eti śarvarīm
english: Having laid out his nooses of sinew duly there, he would go home and sleep at ease while the night wore on toward dawn.

sanskrit: tatra sma nityaṃ badhyante naktaṃ bahuvidhā mṛgāḥ kadā cit tatra mārjāras tv apramatto 'py abadhyata
english: There every night beasts of many kinds were caught; and once the cat, careful though he was, was nonetheless ensnared.

sanskrit: tasmin baddhe mahāprājñaḥ śatrau nityātatāyini taṃ kālaṃ palito jñātvā vicacāra sunirbhayaḥ
english: When that enemy, his perpetual would-be slayer, was thus bound, the very wise Palita, recognizing the moment, roamed about quite free of fear.

sanskrit: tenānucaratā tasmin vane viśvastacāriṇā bhakṣaṃ vicaramāṇena nacirād dṛṣṭam āmiṣam
english: As he ranged through that forest, moving in confidence and questing for food, before long he caught sight of a piece of meat.

sanskrit: sa tam unmātham āruhya tad āmiṣam abhakṣayat tasyopari sapatnasya baddhasya manasā hasan
english: Climbing up onto the very snare, he began to eat that meat, laughing in his heart at his rival caught above him.

sanskrit: āmiṣe tu prasaktaḥ sa kadā cid avalokayan apaśyad aparaṃ ghoram ātmanaḥ śatrum āgatam
english: But while he was intent upon the meat, glancing about at one point he saw another, fearsome enemy of his drawing near.

sanskrit: śaraprasūnasaṃkāśaṃ mahīvivaraśāyinam nakulaṃ harikaṃ nāma capalaṃ tāmralocanam
english: It was a mongoose named Harika—the color of an arrow's reed-blossom, a dweller in burrows of the earth, quick-moving and copper-eyed.

sanskrit: tena mūṣakagandhena tvaramāṇam upāgatam bhakṣārthaṃ lelihad vaktraṃ bhūmāv ūrdhvamukhaṃ sthitam
english: Drawn in haste by the scent of the mouse, it had come up eager to feed, licking its mouth and standing on the ground with face upturned.

sanskrit: śākhāgatam ariṃ cānyad apaśyat koṭarālayam ulūkaṃ candrakaṃ nāma tīkṣṇatuṇḍaṃ kṣapācaram
english: And on a branch he saw yet another foe, lodged in a hollow—an owl named Candraka, sharp of beak and a prowler of the night.

sanskrit: gatasya viṣayaṃ tasya nakulolūkayos tadā athāsyāsīd iyaṃ cintā tat prāpya sumahad bhayam
english: Having come within reach of both the mongoose and the owl, and seized then by very great fear, this thought arose in him:

sanskrit: āpady asyāṃ sukaṣṭāyāṃ maraṇe samupasthite samantād bhaya utpanne kathaṃ kāryaṃ hitaiṣiṇā
english: "In this most grievous calamity, with death close at hand and terror sprung up on every side—how is one who seeks his own welfare to act?"

sanskrit: sa tathā sarvato ruddhaḥ sarvatra samadarśanaḥ abhavad bhayasaṃtaptaś cakre cemāṃ parāṃ gatim
english: Thus blocked on all sides, seeing danger alike in every quarter, he was tormented by fear, and he resolved upon this supreme course.

sanskrit: āpad vināśabhūyiṣṭhā śataikīyaṃ ca jīvitam samantasaṃśayā ceyam asmān āpad upasthitā
english: "This calamity is all but ruin, and life hangs on the slimmest chance; perilous on every side, this distress has come upon me."

sanskrit: gataṃ hi sahasā bhūmiṃ nakulo māṃ samāpnuyāt ulūkaś ceha tiṣṭhantaṃ mārjāraḥ pāśasaṃkṣayāt
english: "If I dart down to the ground, the mongoose will have me; the owl, if I stay here; and the cat, once free of the snare."

sanskrit: na tv evāsmadvidhaḥ prājñaḥ saṃmohaṃ gantum arhati kariṣye jīvite yatnaṃ yāvad ucchvāsanigraham
english: "Yet a wise one such as I ought not give way to confusion. I will strive for my life so long as I can hold my breath."

sanskrit: na hi buddhyānvitāḥ prājñā nītiśāstraviśāradāḥ saṃbhramanty āpadaṃ prāpya mahato 'rthān avāpya ca
english: "For the wise, endowed with understanding and versed in the science of policy, do not lose their heads on meeting calamity, or even on gaining great fortunes."

sanskrit: na tv anyām iha mārjārād gatiṃ paśyāmi sāṃpratam viṣamastho hy ayaṃ jantuḥ kṛtyaṃ cāsya mahan mayā
english: "Yet at this moment I see no refuge here other than the cat; for this creature too stands in difficulty, and he has great need of me."

sanskrit: jīvitārthī kathaṃ tv adya prārthitaḥ śatrubhis tribhiḥ tasmād imam ahaṃ śatruṃ mārjāraṃ saṃśrayāmi vai
english: "How, desiring to live, am I today hunted by three enemies? Therefore I shall take refuge with this very foe, the cat."

sanskrit: kṣatravidyāṃ samāśritya hitam asyopadhāraye yenemaṃ śatrusaṃghātaṃ matipūrveṇa vañcaye
english: "Resorting to the lore of statecraft, I shall point out what is for his good, by which means I may, through deliberate cunning, baffle this assembly of enemies."

sanskrit: ayam atyantaśatrur me vaiṣamyaṃ paramaṃ gataḥ mūḍho grāhayituṃ svārthaṃ saṃgatyā yadi śakyate
english: "This utter enemy of mine has fallen into the gravest of straits; he is bewildered—if by circumstance he can be made to grasp his own interest..."

sanskrit: kadā cid vyasanaṃ prāpya saṃdhiṃ kuryān mayā saha balinā saṃniviṣṭasya śatror api parigrahaḥ kārya ity āhur ācāryā viṣame jīvitārthinā
english: "...then, having met with disaster, he may make a treaty with me. The teachers say that even the embrace of a powerful enemy who has come close should be made by one in difficulty who longs to live."

sanskrit: śreyān hi paṇḍitaḥ śatrur na ca mitram apaṇḍitam mama hy amitre mārjāre jīvitaṃ saṃpratiṣṭhitam
english: "For a wise enemy is better than a foolish friend; indeed, my very life now rests upon my enemy, the cat."

sanskrit: hantainaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi hetum ātmābhirakṣaṇe apīdānīm ayaṃ śatruḥ saṃgatyā paṇḍito bhavet
english: "Come, I shall lay before him a reason touching his own preservation; perhaps now, through these circumstances, this enemy may turn prudent."

sanskrit: tato 'rthagatitattvajñaḥ saṃdhivigrahakālavit sāntvapūrvam idaṃ vākyaṃ mārjāraṃ mūṣako 'bravīt
english: Then the mouse, who knew the true course of interests and the seasons for peace and for war, addressed the cat with these conciliatory words:

sanskrit: sauhṛdenābhibhāṣe tvā kaccin mārjāra jīvasi jīvitaṃ hi tavecchāmi śreyaḥ sādhāraṇaṃ hi nau
english: "In friendship I speak to you, O cat. Are you still alive? I do desire your life, for our welfare lies in common."

sanskrit: na te saumya viṣattavyaṃ jīviṣyasi yathā purā ahaṃ tvām uddhariṣyāmi prāṇāñ jahyāṃ hi te kṛte
english: "You need not despair, good friend; you shall live as before. I will deliver you—indeed I would lay down my own life for your sake."

sanskrit: asti kaś cid upāyo 'tra puṣkalaḥ pratibhāti mām yena śakyas tvayā mokṣaḥ prāptuṃ śreyo yathā mayā
english: "There is, it seems to me, a sound and ample means by which you may win your release, just as I may win my safety."

sanskrit: mayā hy upāyo dṛṣṭo 'yaṃ vicārya matim ātmanaḥ ātmārthaṃ ca tvadarthaṃ ca śreyaḥ sādhāraṇaṃ hi nau
english: "I have hit upon this device, having reasoned it through in my own mind, for my sake and for yours alike; for our good is shared."

sanskrit: idaṃ hi nakulolūkaṃ pāpabuddhy abhitaḥ sthitam na dharṣayati mārjāra tena me svasti sāṃpratam
english: "This mongoose and this owl, malicious of mind, stand near me on either side. So long, O cat, as one does not assail me, I am for the moment safe."

sanskrit: kūjaṃś capalanetro 'yaṃ kauśiko māṃ nirīkṣate nagaśākhāgrahas tiṣṭhaṃs tasyāhaṃ bhṛśam udvije
english: "Hooting, with restless eyes, this owl is watching me from where it perches on a branch of the tree; of it I am sorely afraid."

sanskrit: satāṃ sāptapadaṃ sakhyaṃ savāso me 'si paṇḍitaḥ sāṃvāsyakaṃ kariṣyāmi nāsti te mṛtyuto bhayam
english: "Among the good, friendship is sealed by seven steps together; you are my fellow-dweller and a wise one. I will make a true companionship of it—you have no cause to fear death."

sanskrit: na hi śaknoṣi mārjāra pāśaṃ chettuṃ vinā mayā ahaṃ chetsyāmi te pāśaṃ yadi māṃ tvaṃ na hiṃsasi
english: "For you, O cat, cannot cut the noose without me. I will cut your noose, if you do not harm me."

sanskrit: tvam āśrito nagasyāgraṃ mūlaṃ tv aham upāśritaḥ ciroṣitāv ihāvāṃ vai vṛkṣe 'smin viditaṃ hi te
english: "You dwell in the tree's crown, and I at its root. The two of us have long lived here in this very tree, as you well know."

sanskrit: yasminn āśvasate kaś cid yaś ca nāśvasate kva cit na tau dhīrāḥ praśaṃsanti nityam udvignacetasau
english: "One who trusts no one at all, and one in whom no one ever trusts—the wise praise neither, for both are forever uneasy of heart."

sanskrit: tasmād vivardhatāṃ prītiḥ satyā saṃgatir astu nau kālātītam apārthaṃ hi na praśaṃsanti paṇḍitāḥ
english: "Therefore let our friendship grow, and let there be a true union between us; for the wise do not commend an act that is purposeless and let slip its proper time."

sanskrit: arthayuktim imāṃ tāvad yathābhūtāṃ niśāmaya tava jīvitam icchāmi tvaṃ mamecchasi jīvitam
english: "Mark, then, this reasoning of interest just as it stands: I desire your life, and you desire mine."

sanskrit: kaś cit tarati kāṣṭhena sugambhīrāṃ mahānadīm sa tārayati tat kāṣṭhaṃ sa ca kāṣṭhena tāryate
english: "A man crosses a deep, great river by means of a log; he carries the log across, and he in turn is carried across by the log."

sanskrit: īdṛśo nau samāyogo bhaviṣyati sunistaraḥ ahaṃ tvāṃ tārayiṣyāmi tvaṃ ca māṃ tārayiṣyasi
english: "Such will be our compact, and it shall carry us safely through: I will bring you across, and you will bring me across."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu palitas tadartham ubhayor hitam hetumad grahaṇīyaṃ ca kālākāṅkṣī vyapaikṣata
english: Having spoken thus to that end, for the good of both, Palita—his argument cogent and fit to be accepted—bided his time and watched.

sanskrit: atha suvyāhṛtaṃ tasya śrutvā śatrur vicakṣaṇaḥ hetumad grahaṇīyārthaṃ mārjāro vākyam abravīt
english: Then, hearing his well-spoken words, the cat, his discerning enemy, made this reply—reasoned and worthy of acceptance:

sanskrit: buddhimān vākyasaṃpannas tad vākyam anuvarṇayan tām avasthām avekṣyāntyāṃ sāmnaiva pratyapūjayat
english: Intelligent and gifted in speech, dwelling on those words and looking to his own desperate plight, he received them graciously, with conciliation alone.

sanskrit: tatas tīkṣṇāgradaśano vaiḍūryamaṇilocanaḥ mūṣakaṃ mandam udvīkṣya mārjāro lomaśo 'bravīt
english: Then the cat Lomaśa, his teeth keen at the tips and his eyes like beryl gems, gazed gently down at the mouse and said:

sanskrit: nandāmi saumya bhadraṃ te yo māṃ jīvantam icchasi śreyaś ca yadi jānīṣe kriyatāṃ mā vicāraya
english: "I rejoice, good friend—blessings on you—that you wish me to live. And if you know the way to our good, let it be done; do not hesitate."

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi dṛḍham āpannas tvam āpannataro mayā dvayor āpannayoḥ saṃdhiḥ kriyatāṃ mā vicāraya
english: "For I am sorely fallen into distress, and you are in even worse straits than I. Let a treaty be made between the two of us in distress; do not hesitate."

sanskrit: vidhatsva prāptakālaṃ yat kāryaṃ sidhyatu cāvayoḥ mayi kṛcchrād vinirmukte na vinaṅkṣyati te kṛtam
english: "Do what the moment demands, and let our undertaking succeed for us both. Once I am freed from this peril, your good deed shall not be lost."

sanskrit: nyastamāno 'smi bhakto 'smi śiṣyas tvaddhitakṛt tathā nideśavaśavartī ca bhavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
english: "My pride is laid aside; I am devoted to you, your disciple, a doer of your bidding, obedient to your command; I have come to you for refuge."

sanskrit: ity evam uktaḥ palito mārjāraṃ vaśam āgatam vākyaṃ hitam uvācedam abhinītārtham arthavat
english: Thus addressed, Palito spoke this salutary word to the cat, now brought under his sway—a word fitly framed and full of meaning:

sanskrit: udāraṃ yad bhavān āha naitac citraṃ bhavadvidhe vidito yas tu mārgo me hitārthaṃ śṛṇu taṃ mama
english: "Noble is what you have said—no wonder in one like you. But hear from me the course I have in mind for our good."

sanskrit: ahaṃ tvānupravekṣyāmi nakulān me mahad bhayam trāyasva māṃ mā vadhīś ca śakto 'smi tava mokṣaṇe
english: "I will creep up close beneath you. From the mongoose comes my great fear. Protect me and do not slay me—I am able to win you your release."

sanskrit: ulūkāc caiva māṃ rakṣa kṣudraḥ prārthayate hi mām ahaṃ chetsyāmi te pāśān sakhe satyena te śape
english: "From the owl as well guard me, for the vile thing covets me. I will cut your nooses, friend—I swear it to you in truth."

sanskrit: tad vacaḥ saṃgataṃ śrutvā lomaśo yuktam arthavat harṣād udvīkṣya palitaṃ svāgatenābhyapūjayat
english: Hearing that speech, coherent and fitting and full of sense, Lomaśa looked up at Palita in joy and welcomed him warmly.

sanskrit: sa taṃ saṃpūjya palitaṃ mārjāraḥ sauhṛde sthitaḥ suvicintyābravīd dhīraḥ prītas tvarita eva hi
english: Having honored Palita, the cat, now set upon friendship, the steady one, after careful thought, spoke—glad, and indeed in haste:

sanskrit: kṣipram āgaccha bhadraṃ te tvaṃ me prāṇasamaḥ sakhā tava prājña prasādād dhi kṣipraṃ prāpsyāmi jīvitam
english: "Come quickly—blessings on you—you are a friend dear to me as life itself. For by your favor, wise one, I shall swiftly regain my life."

sanskrit: yad yad evaṃgatenādya śakyaṃ kartuṃ mayā tava tad ājñāpaya kartāhaṃ saṃdhir evāstu nau sakhe
english: "Whatever I, in this plight, am able to do for you today, command it, and I will do it. Let there be a treaty between us, my friend."

sanskrit: asmāt te saṃśayān muktaḥ samitragaṇabāndhavaḥ sarvakāryāṇi kartāhaṃ priyāṇi ca hitāni ca
english: "Once freed by you from this peril, together with my friends and kin, I will do all your bidding, whatever pleases you and serves your good."

sanskrit: muktaś ca vyasanād asmāt saumyāham api nāma te prītim utpādayeyaṃ ca pratikartuṃ ca śaknuyām
english: "And once delivered from this disaster, good friend, may I too kindle your affection, and may I be able to repay you."

sanskrit: grāhayitvā tu taṃ svārthaṃ mārjāraṃ mūṣakas tadā praviveśa suvisrabdhaḥ samyag arthāṃś cacāra ha
english: Having made the cat grasp where his own interest lay, the mouse then crept up in full confidence and conducted the business aright.

sanskrit: evam āśvāsito vidvān mārjāreṇa sa mūṣakaḥ mārjārorasi visrabdhaḥ suṣvāpa pitṛmātṛvat
english: Thus reassured by the cat, that learned mouse slept trustingly upon the cat's breast, as upon a father's or a mother's.
